symptom: a weak stream and getting up at night to pee
hook: both drainage pipes from the kidneys had ballooned into twisting garden hoses
whatYouSee: Both kidneys have swollen drainage systems and both ureters are wide and twisted down to a large rounded bladder.
whyItMatters: When outflow from the bladder is blocked the back pressure dilates both ureters and both kidney collecting systems. Left untreated this can damage kidney function.
treatment: Treatment targets the blockage and may include bladder drainage with a catheter and later relief of the obstruction. Upper tract drainage such as percutaneous nephrostomy or ureteric stenting may be needed.
takeaway: When both sides are dilated look below the ureters at the bladder and its outlet.

findings: Projection: Anteroposterior (AP) plain radiograph of the abdomen and pelvis, intravenous urogram (IVU) phase

Bilateral renal collecting systems opacified with contrast: the left kidney demonstrates markedly enlarged, rounded calyces with clubbing and loss of the normal papillary impressions, consistent with calyceal dilatation; the right kidney shows similar but less pronounced calyceal blunting and dilatation
Bilateral ureters are opacified and demonstrate a markedly tortuous, serpentine course from the renal pelves to the bladder, with multiple redundant loops along their entire length
The urinary bladder is opacified and appears markedly enlarged, smoothly rounded, and centrally positioned within the pelvis, with a large ovoid contrast-filled lumen
Lumbar spine is visible in the midline; mild degenerative changes noted at multiple levels
Pelvic bones and hip joints appear grossly intact bilaterally
No obvious radiopaque calculi identified along the urinary tract
Soft tissue shadows are otherwise unremarkable on this radiograph
differential: Chronic bladder outlet obstruction (e.g., benign prostatic hyperplasia or urethral stricture) with bilateral hydroureteronephrosis: the massively distended bladder, bilateral ureteral tortuosity, and calyceal dilatation are classic for long-standing lower urinary tract obstruction

Primary megaureter (bilateral) with secondary pelvicalyceal dilatation: congenital or acquired bilateral ureteral aperistalsis or distal obstruction producing the marked serpentine ureteral redundancy seen

Neurogenic bladder with bilateral vesicoureteral reflux: a large atonic bladder with bilateral dilated tortuous ureters and calyceal clubbing can result from neurogenic dysfunction and chronic reflux nephropathy
anatomyConcerns: The degree of ureteral tortuosity is extreme and bilateral, which is a pathological finding rather than normal anatomy
The bladder size is markedly enlarged beyond normal capacity, indicating pathological retention or atonia
Left renal collecting system appears more severely dilated than right, raising concern for asymmetric obstruction or differential renal function
Calyceal clubbing on the left suggests established parenchymal damage (reflux nephropathy or chronic obstruction)

imageApproval.diagnosticReason: The IVU film shows bilateral dilated tortuous ureters with serpentine redundant loops from renal pelvis to bladder, bilateral calyceal blunting and clubbing (left greater than right), and a massively distended smooth-walled bladder. The clinical vignette of weak stream and nocturia in an older adult points to bladder outlet obstruction as the underlying cause, producing the classic bilateral hydroureteronephrosis pattern. No calcified stones are visible. The independent differential lists chronic outlet obstruction as the top candidate, which is entirely consistent with the vignette. No alternative diagnosis is equally or better supported when the clinical context is applied.
